finding.claim: The unauthenticated POST /hooks/test route passes the request body's `callback` value straight to axios.post. An anonymous attacker can make the server send POST requests to any URL, including internal services and cloud metadata endpoints. Only the response status is returned (semi-blind), but that still gives an internal port and host oracle, and the POST can trigger state-changing internal endpoints. axios follows redirects by default, so a redirect from an attacker-hosted URL can also reach internal hosts.

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') handler registered on the `pub` router with no auth middleware (only `admin` router uses requireAdmin)
req.body.callback passed unvalidated as the URL to axios.post
The upstream response status is returned to the caller, giving a reachability oracle

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP blocking, DNS pinning, or redirect restriction. requireAdmin is applied only to the `admin` router (routes.js:12), not `pub`. I could not see how `pub` is mounted because routes.js is the only file in the directory, so any auth middleware applied at mount time is unchecked. No body validation is present.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 registers pub.post('/hooks/test') with no auth middleware (requireAdmin is only on admin at routes.js:12) and passes req.body.callback unvalidated to axios.post at routes.js:20, returning the status at routes.js:21; the mount point is not in the directory, so auth applied there is unchecked, but nothing in the code available restricts it.

finding.claim: GET /diagnostics/fetch passes req.query.url unvalidated to axios.get. This is a classic SSRF, but it sits behind requireAdmin, so it needs admin privilege. I am reporting it as low-confidence and probably out of scope, because it does not appear to grant more than an admin already holds.
finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) is enforced with a return on failure. There is no URL validation, no IP blocking, and redirects are followed. Exploitation requires an admin session, or a separate way to forge one.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12) is an auth guard, not a URL guard. There is no URL validation.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12 and :15), but the sink at routes.js:15 can only be reached through admin.use(requireAdmin) (routes.js:7-12), which returns 403 unless session.role is "admin". An unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker therefore cannot control the URL, so the source is not attacker-controllable.
